title: method-cards
description: The method-selection catalogue: one card per method family, carrying the guidance a user needs to choose between them. The SHA-256 sidecar beside this artifact proves it is the file that was sealed; this schema proves it is the right SHAPE, which a fresh digest over a wrong file does not. Every field below was read off the artifact on disk, not recalled: `additionalProperties: false` on a card is therefore load-bearing, because it is what catches a field being reintroduced, renamed or invented.

node_specs_sha256.description: Pins this catalogue to one exact node-specs.json. The two artifacts are a matched pair and a card that describes nodes which no longer exist is worse than no card at all.

reseal.description: The bytes this artifact superseded, and why. The re-seal of box 2.1.15 happened IN PLACE -- same filenames, same seven sidecars, wrapper_file untouched because mcp/gateway.py and naming.py join on it -- so without this block it would leave no trace at all. The digests are the ones the sidecars carried before the re-seal; they are authored in corpus/_provenance.json rather than read from git, because .dockerignore excludes .git/ and the image build runs the generator's own suite. The same record is emitted onto node-specs.json and method-cards.json: one re-seal, one record.

wrapper_file.description: The module that implements this card's methods. naming.py and the gateway join on this value, so a card pointing at a module that does not exist breaks routing rather than merely misinforming a reader.

tool_fns.description: The wire function names this card covers. Never empty: a card that routes to nothing cannot be recommended.

alternatives.description: Where to go instead, and the criterion that sends you there. A bare list of method names would be useless guidance, so each entry carries both halves and both are required.

chart_kind.description: The single chart a client draws for this card's PRINCIPAL result, derived from output_key_fields and the method text. AUTHORED, not derived: nothing in the tree can compute which chart a result deserves. `none` is a real answer for a card that produces nothing to display -- file and format I/O, calendars, parsers, schema verdicts, handles -- and is never a way of avoiding a decision. The enum repeats node-specs.json's `chart_kinds` vocabulary, which is where the closed set is declared; tests/test_chart_map.py asserts every node resolves to a member of it and that no member is dead.

sources.description: Academic citations. Null is permitted and is measured: exactly one card carries no source today. It is not the same as an empty list, which would assert that the question was asked and answered with nothing.

precondition_tools.description: Diagnostics to run before trusting this method. Null where the question does not arise; a list where it does.

precondition_gates.description: The cross-cutting gates a body must run before trusting its input, named by the detail code the refusal carries. CLOSED: every entry resolves through gates/registry.py PRIMITIVES, and tests/test_chart_map.py asserts this enum, that registry and corpus/_vocabulary.json are one set. Null on every card today; prose describing what a wrapper validates belongs in validation_notes.

validation_notes.description: What this card's methods check about their own arguments and results, in prose, one sentence per note. Filesystem state, argument grammar, membership against a runtime list, a security ordering, a post-condition, a default: requirements that are real and documented and that no closed vocabulary of cross-cutting numeric gates can name. Null where the question does not arise.

embed_text.description: The retrieval text, rebuilt from the fields above rather than hand-written, so it cannot drift away from the card it describes.
